content: The mandibular and hyoid arches develop at a faster rate compared to the arches located posterior to them. As a result, the posterior arches become partially enclosed within the anterior ones, leading to the formation of a pronounced depression on each side of the neck, known as the cervical sinus. This cervical sinus is anatomically bordered anteriorly by the hyoid arch and posteriorly by the thoracic wall. Over time, the walls of the cervical sinus fuse together, leading to its eventual obliteration.
